issues.descricao: The first-record check is `activeEntries.length === 1 && entries.length === 1`, so it counts records, not days. When someone with several indicators fills in their first day, they make several records and never see the thank-you. `PanelSummary` ('N registros no seu histórico') shows up instead. The test 'first filling with several indicators is acknowledged until a second day is recorded' in `e2e/empty-dashboard-regressions.spec.ts` expects the thank-you after two records on the same day, which contradicts this logic. The code only satisfies the single-indicator case (`empty-dashboard.spec.ts`). Also, `localDate` is loaded by `listEntryDates` and never used.
issues.sugestao: Work out the first day from the distinct `localDate` values of active entries (`new Set(activeEntries.map(e => e.localDate)).size === 1`) and decide whether archived entries count. Confirm that the regressions spec really runs in G6. As written, it should fail.

issues.descricao: `countEntries` and `countActiveIndicators` (`getCountFromServer`) were added but nothing uses them. This is dead code, and it goes against AGENTS.md's rule to prefer minimal code.
issues.sugestao: Remove both functions and their imports (`getCountFromServer`, `where`).

issues.descricao: Every dashboard load reads all of the user's entries through REST (paged at 300) just to decide between the empty, no-records and first-record states. The cost grows with the size of the history. Also, the comment 'Aggregation queries are one-shot' does not describe the code: it does a full list, not an aggregation.
issues.sugestao: Limit the read (for example, a query with limit 2 or one ordered by `localDate`) or use aggregation and an existence check. Fix the comment.

issues.descricao: `addSuggestion` adds 1 to `activeIndicatorCount` even when `createSuggestedIndicator` returns true because the document already existed (for example, it was created in another tab). The local counter can drift.
issues.sugestao: Only add to the counter when the key was not already in `createdKeys`, or have the function tell you whether it created the document.

issues.descricao: The initial-state `useEffect` resets roughly 7 states twice, once for each branch. The page is about 450 lines, with several sub-components that are only used here. This is verbose given the minimal-code rule.
issues.sugestao: Group the loaded data into a single state object (`useState<DashboardData | null>`) to cut down the resets.
